items.headline: 6.8 quake in Indian Ocean, no tsunami threat
items.summary: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck the Indian Ocean in Indonesian waters around 3:12 PM at a depth of about 156 km. The Department of Meteorology issued a bulletin at 3:30 PM saying Sri Lanka faces no tsunami threat.

items.headline: Deduru Oya spill gates opened after heavy rain
items.summary: Four sluice gates were raised by a foot each, releasing about 2,800 cubic feet of water per second. People living downstream are asked to stay alert and watch river levels.

items.headline: 21 Jaffna University students remanded after clash
items.summary: A dispute between second- and third-year Commerce and Management students turned violent, leaving three hospitalised with cuts. The 21 arrested students were remanded until 26 November by the Jaffna Magistrate.

items.headline: Dayasiri questions mandatory remand rules
items.summary: In Parliament, MP Dayasiri Jayasekara challenged Anti-Corruption Act provisions that restrict bail once the bribery commission's certificate is filed, citing Namal Rajapaksa's case. He warned the government against using the law against political opponents.

items.headline: PM denies education cuts in Budget 2027
items.summary: During the Committee Stage debate, PM Harini Amarasuriya rejected opposition claims of reduced education spending. She pointed to wider Suraksha insurance cover and higher Mahapola and student allowances.

items.headline: Over 70 wanted suspects brought back from abroad
items.summary: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala said more than 70 organised crime suspects hiding overseas have been repatriated. He spoke at an STF passing-out parade in Katukurunda.

items.headline: Committee urges EV battery recycling system
items.summary: The Committee on Ways and Means said importers and manufacturers should be made responsible for disposing of used electric vehicle batteries. It also discussed customs delays and EV tax incentives.

items.headline: Trade deals and tariffs reviewed in Parliament
items.summary: The same committee reviewed tariff policy and ongoing trade negotiations with the Department of Commerce. It called for feasibility studies on agreements still being negotiated.

items.headline: New Colombo apartment complexes planned by 2027
items.summary: The NHDA will work with private developers on new urban housing. Deputy Minister T.B. Sarath inspected state land in Colombo and ordered fixes at the Jana Sevana complex in Dematagoda.

items.headline: Diesel leak at Bloemendhal fuel terminal
items.summary: Diesel leaked from the storage terminal into nearby drains this morning. Residents were seen collecting the spilled fuel in containers.

items.headline: Two feared drowned off Nintavur
items.summary: Two young men went missing while bathing in the sea at Nintavur, and a search is under way.

items.headline: Thalawathugoda scrap yard fire contained
items.summary: The fire at the scrap metal yard reported this morning has been brought under control.

items.headline: Lightning warning for 13 districts
items.summary: An amber warning covers Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Kegalle, Nuwara Eliya, Puttalam and Ratnapura, plus parts of six other districts. It stays in force until 1 AM tomorrow.

items.headline: Sri Lanka lose Test series in Pakistan
items.summary: Pakistan won the second Test in Rawalpindi by eight wickets to take the series 1-0. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 98 in their first innings.

items.headline: Trinity in command after Senarathne's 160
items.summary: A big 160 by Senarathne has put Trinity College in a strong position in their school cricket match.

items.headline: EU and UK sign deal to strengthen post-Brexit ties
items.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom announced what they called a landmark agreement to deepen relations.
